acme_netops: Hey team — since yesterday our app can't complete requests to the private Redwood endpoint behind our corp LB. Seeing TLS handshake failures 50% of the time

acme_netops: curl -v output attached, shows 'SSL: error:1408A0C1:SSL routines:ssl3_get_client_hello:no shared cipher'

maria_support: sorry to hear that — can you paste the full curl -v and also the output of `openssl s_client -connect <endpoint>:443 -servername <hostname> -alpn h2`? and which cert type are you terminating at the LB (RSA vs ECDSA)?

acme_netops: LB terminates TLS and we use ECDSA leaf certs. here's a sanitized s_client run:

```
$ openssl s_client -connect redwood-private.acme:443 -servername redwood-private.acme -alpn h2
CONNECTED(00000003)
139826...:error:1408A0C1:SSL routines:ssl3_get_client_hello:no shared cipher:ssl/ssl_statem.c:??
---
no peer certificate available
---
```

acme_netops: Our LB had a recent config push to prefer ECDSA-only ciphers + TLS1.3. Backend health checks sometimes succeed but downstream TLS to Redwood fails.

josh_se: thanks. two likely vectors: 1) ALPN/cipher mismatch where LB offers only TLS1.3+ECDSA-only suites but Redwood runtime also requires RSA fallback for some older nodes, or 2) client (your app) isn't sending SNI the same way the LB expects. Do you have a capture from the LB for the TLS ClientHello?

acme_netops: I can get VM tcpdump of ClientHello. Quick question — does Redwood require RSA certs anywhere for VPC endpoints? We used ECDSA everywhere so far.

maria_support: our Private control plane supports both ECDSA and RSA cert chains, but some downstream internal components (legacy autoscaler / health probes) historically preferred RSA. That said, the error 'no shared cipher' suggests the LB and Redwood couldn't agree on a cipher suite list. If you can get the ClientHello we can confirm cipher list and extensions (SNI, ALPN, signature_algorithms).

dave_infra: copying some quick commands you can run from the LB node to debug: 

```
# show cipher suites client offers
openssl ciphers -v 'ALL:eNULL' | sed -n '1,40p'

# test TLS1.2/RSA handshake
openssl s_client -connect redwood-private.acme:443 -servername redwood-private.acme -tls1_2 -cipher 'ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384'

# test TLS1.3 suite
openssl s_client -connect redwood-private.acme:443 -servername redwood-private.acme -tls1_3 -ciphersuites TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
```

acme_netops: ran the TLS1.2 test, got certificate chain back but the TLS1.3 test failed with 'no shared cipher'. here's the LB config snippet that was rolled out:

```
ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
ssl_prefer_server_ciphers on;
ssl_ciphers 'ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256';
```

acme_netops: We were trying to tighten the profile, but looks like Redwood endpoints prefer a broader set.

josh_se: that config is ECDSA-only ciphers and disables RSA suites. If any path (health checker, older proxy hop inside Redwood private tenancy, or some of our middleboxes) advertises RSA-only or expects RSA-signed certs, the handshake can fail. Two practical fixes: 1) add RSA suites back into ssl_ciphers or 2) configure LB to present a cert chain that includes an RSA-signed chain (or use dual certs).

maria_support: also check ALPN — our runtime expects h2 or http/1.1. If LB strips ALPN or rewrites it, connection can fall back in odd ways. Can you run `tcpdump -s 0 -A -w /tmp/hello.pcap 'tcp port 443 and host <redwood-ip>'` and share the ClientHello bytes?

acme_netops: uploading pcap to our S3, link shared in DM. Quick patch: we re-enabled RSA suites and the failure rate dropped to ~0-1%.

dave_infra: good sign. For long term: recommend one of these options:
- Keep LB ECDSA-only but present a certificate chain that has an RSA alternative for clients that need it (many vendors support dual cert selection)
- Re-add RSA suites with appropriate ordering (ECDHE-ECDSA first) so you retain ECDSA preference but allow RSA fallback
- If you can, enable TLS debug/logging on the LB to capture exact ClientHello/CipherList on rejects and confirm ALPN/SNI are present

maria_support: I'll note this as "TLS profile mismatch — corp LB prefers ECDSA-only, Redwood endpoints require RSA fallback for some internal paths" and attach the commands + our suggested config. Marking as resolved pending your confirmation after 24h. :thumbsup:

acme_netops: thanks all — re-enabled RSA suites for now. Will test for 24h and report back. Appreciate the quick triage.

ingress-bot: Incident note created: #INC-2026-1421 — TLS negotiation failures for acme private endpoint. Assigned to josh_se and dave_infra.
